caption:
A UCSF team (Chang lab) used a high-density ECoG implant with machine-learning decoders so paralysed participants could speak and gesture, such as nodding and waving, through an avatar at the same time. Three participants, two in real time, restricted vocabulary, wired, in a lab. Brosler et al., Nature Neuroscience, 14 Sept 2026.

#neuroscience #bci #science #neurotech
voiceover_script: Paralysed and unable to speak. Their avatar talks and waves, straight from their brain. This is a brain-computer interface from the Chang lab at UCSF. A high-density implant called ECoG records signals from the brain. Machine-learning decoders turn those signals into speech and into gestures, like nodding and waving, and an on-screen avatar performs both at the same time. Now the honest part. Three participants, two of them driving the avatar in real time, with a restricted vocabulary, over a wired connection, in a lab. This is a demonstration, not a treatment you can go and get. But it is the first time speech and gestures have been decoded together like this. Nature Neuroscience, fourteenth of September. Source in the caption.
